identity.title: The VLA View of the HL Tau Disk: Disk Mass, Grain Evolution, and Early Planet Formation

paper_type_evidence.quote: Here, we present the most sensitive images of HL Tau obtained to date with the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array at 7.0 mm wavelength with a spatial resolution comparable to the ALMA images.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00015.SV.

question.value: What do new deep VLA 7.0 mm images of the HL Tau disk, which are optically thin, reveal about disk dust mass, grain growth and early planet formation, compared with the ALMA images?

evidence.quote: At this long wavelength the dust emission from HL Tau is optically thin, allowing a comprehensive study of the inner disk.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00015.SV.

method.value: CLEAN multi-scale MFS, varying robust and uv-taper; also two 4 GHz sub-bands

evidence.quote: We also made images by splitting the 8 GHz band in two sub-bands of 4 GHz each (central wavelengths 6.7 and 7.3 mm).

method.value: Average intensity in 0.01 arcsec wide elliptical rings using IRING on images aligned and convolved to 0.07 arcsec

evidence.quote: we obtained the average intensity within concentric elliptical rings of 0$\ensuremath{''}$01 width at different radii, using the task `IRING`

method.value: Extrapolate jet flux from 6 and 2 cm with spectral index 0.4 (upper limit) or -0.1 from 2 cm (lower limit)

evidence.quote: an upper limit to the free-free contribution at 7.0 mm is obtained by extrapolating the flux density from cm wavelengths with a spectral index of 0.4

validation.value: Compared with spectral index from 6.7 and 7.3 mm sub-bands (~1 at disk center)

evidence.quote: we obtain a spectral index of $\sim$1 at the center of the disk

analysis_steps.goal: Derive Tb, spectral indices, optical depth, column density and dust mass

method.value: Planck brightness temperature; spectral indices; optical depth and column density from power-law dust temperature and opacity; masses by integrating column density between dark rings

evidence.quote: we obtain first estimates by assuming a simple power-law for the dust temperature in the form $T_{dust}=T_{0} (R/R_{0})^{-q}$.
with different proposed values in the range $T_0\simeq$70-140 K at $R_0$=10 au

validation.value: Compared with Pinte et al. (2016) masses for optically thin ALMA rings B2-B6

evidence.quote: we obtain dust masses consistent with previous estimations (Pinte et al. 2016)
Calibration of the data was performed with the data reduction package Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA; version 4.4.0)
using the task `IRING` of the Astronomical Image Processing System (AIPS)
the total dust mass of the disk is within the range (1-3)$\times$10$^{-3}$ M$_\ensuremath{\odot}$

findings_qualitative.value: 7.0 mm emission is optically thin at all radii (tau ≲ 0.4), unlike ALMA wavelengths

evidence.quote: This imply that dust emission at 7.0 mm is well optically thin at all radii, even in the densest parts of the disk.

claims.hypothesis: Is the HL Tau inner disk optically thin at 7 mm, allowing mass determination?
claims.experiment: Compared 7.0 mm VLA brightness temperatures with ALMA 0.87 mm
claims.result: Tb ~45 and 15 K vs ~130 and 60 K; tau ≲0.4 at 7 mm
claims.finding: Emission optically thin; total dust mass (1-3)e-3 Msun, larger than earlier estimates

evidence.quote: we obtain optical depths $\lesssim$0.4 at 7.0 mm.

claims.hypothesis: Does grain size vary with radius?

evidence.quote: a clear gradient in $\alpha_{7.0-2.9mm}$ is observed between $\sim$10-50 au

claims.hypothesis: Is there a dust clump in the first bright ring?
claims.experiment: Multiple images of B1 at 7 mm
claims.result: Compact NE knot persistent in all images, alpha=2.5±0.4
claims.finding: Likely a dense dust clump; planets may be forming in the bright rings

evidence.loc: 3.3 Substructure in the first bright ring
evidence.quote: All this suggests that the 7.0 mm NE knot traces a real structure in the first bright ring.

why_this_data.value: Longer wavelength gives lower optical depth in the inner disk

evidence.quote: The challenge of deriving density profiles and grain size distributions can only be circumvented by observations at even longer wavelengths where the disk will be optically thinner.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: NE knot brightening from jet free-free emission considered but disfavored

evidence.loc: 3.3 Substructure in the first bright ring
evidence.quote: at 7.0 mm, the free-free emission from the jet is expected to be confined within the inner disk

limitations_admitted.value: Mass estimates are rough; detailed radiative transfer modeling needed; free-free correction adds uncertainty at the center

evidence.quote: An accurate determination of the mass distribution in the HL Tau disk requires detailed radiative transfer modeling.
